_meta.title: Core grapheme-phoneme correspondences
_meta.description: The most common sound(s) for core graphemes, each ordered by frequency (most common first) and, where relevant, conditioned on position/context. Frequency-ORDERED per-grapheme sound lists are a legal pure-grapheme tiebreak (a property of the letter, not the word); a whole-word pronunciation lookup is not.
_meta.source_notes: Empirical grapheme-phoneme probabilities: Berndt, Reggia & Mitchum (1987); Gontijo et al. (2003). Position/rime conditioning: Kessler & Treiman (2001, 2003); Siegelman et al. (2020). Soft/hard c & g and positional rules: Orton-Gillingham tradition.
_meta.status: seed — a small correct core; expand toward the full ~44-phoneme inventory and their graphemes
_meta.notation: IPA in slashes; 'short'/'long' noted where the diacritic matters. Positions: initial | medial | final | before-e/i/y | after-short-vowel.

sounds.condition: before e, i, or y (soft c)
often before e, i, or y (soft g)

final_k.rule: /k/ is spelled 'ck' after a single short vowel in a one-syllable word; 'k' after a consonant or long vowel

floss.rule: double f, l, s (and z) after a single short vowel at the end of a one-syllable base word

tch_dge.rule: /tʃ/ is 'tch' and /dʒ/ is 'dge' right after a single short vowel; else 'ch' / 'ge'

vowelsBySyllableType._note: Syllable type IS the vowel rule: the rime (vowel + following context) sets the sound. Reliable in STRESSED syllables; unstressed vowels reduce to schwa and are not fully rule-governed.
